response.goal: Fix the n8n workflow so the full file of about 5,000 rows lands every night into a Google Sheet without hitting a 429 Too Many Requests error, with retries and a Slack message if it still fails.

plan.step: Audit the existing n8n workflow and the Google Sheets node configuration to identify the rate limit and batching bottlenecks during the nightly import of 5,000 rows
Modify the workflow to split the CSV data into smaller chunks or add rate-limiting delays between requests to prevent 429 Too Many Requests errors
Implement built-in error handling with retries on the Google Sheets node for robust execution
Configure a Slack alert node to trigger if the workflow execution ultimately fails after retries

milestones.name: Audit and Fix
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow with batched processing and retry logic for the Google Sheets node

milestones.name: Testing and Slack Alert
milestones.deliverable: End-to-end test of the nightly import and verified Slack failure notification

risks.risk: Google Sheets API quota limits may still restrict write speeds even with batching.
risks.mitigation: Introduce structured delay nodes or smaller chunk sizes between API calls to stay under rate limits.

risks.risk: The current CSV structure or data format might have changed, contributing to the failure.
risks.mitigation: Perform a test run with a full sample dataset during the initial audit phase.

questions: What is the current batch size or loop structure in the failing n8n workflow?
Do you already have a Slack webhook or channel set up for the alert notification?
assumptions: Access to the existing n8n instance and Google Sheets account will be provided.
